significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that item beliefs factor into state content and a causally distinct temporal-validity index, while "anachronism-rate ... grows with the number of state changes and narrative length" and layerwise separation "predicts anachronistic answers"; this combines a form-(ii) causal decomposition with form-(iii) scaling and predictive relations. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, fixing expectations about which narratives should fail, which internal geometry should precede failure, and why steering time validity can change current-versus-past reports without changing factual content; this is relevant to the time-conditioned knowledge failures measured by TempLAMA (Dhingra et al., TACL 2022) and SituatedQA (Zhang and Choi, EMNLP 2021). True and false are distinguishable, and a negative result would rule out the specific factorized temporal-index explanation, although it would not decide whether other representations cause temporal errors. The topic-substitution check lowers no credit: deleting "temporal-validity direction," its collapse-to-error coupling, and the scaling claim leaves only generic research on LLM beliefs, which would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The claim hands over three named handles: the "anachronism-rate metric," a "temporal-validity direction" usable for causal steering, and separation collapse as a predictor of anachronistic answers. The predictor is ex ante at the answer-generation stage and the direction supplies an inference-time corrective knob, creating an action window before the erroneous report rather than merely explaining it afterward. Although the direction itself must be re-extracted per model, the claimed relations—error growth with state changes and narrative length, plus low current/stale separation predicting errors—would predict what researchers should find after recalibration; asserted scope covers a class of changing-state narratives and LLM families, but not unrelated tasks or modalities. Auditors and deployers of temporally sensitive systems could use the predictor or steering knob, and the topic-substitution check confirms that generic "LLM beliefs" alone supplies neither these handles nor this reach.
